boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the frozen Newtonia record (October 28, 1864) in Price's Missouri Expedition [September-October 1864]. The recall of Sanborn's and McNeil's brigades, the siege of Fayetteville and the pursuit to the Arkansas River are context. Campaign-wide marches, recruiting, destruction, returns and multi-action loss totals are context; they are not assigned to one record or added across records. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. The frozen side-specific numerical strength bounds are blank (missing_numeric_strength). No figure in this pass is adopted as a simultaneous opening force.

claims.value: The frozen force field reads Five brigades and remnants of Price's Army of Missouri; the live field reads zero. Price says Blunt came on with 3,000 cavalry. Britton says Blunt attacked with two small brigades (Ford's two regiments, then Jennison's) of less than two regiments in strength, that Shelby had superior numbers, and that Sanborn's brigade of four Missouri militia regiments and the Second Arkansas arrived before sundown.
claims.rationale: An interested estimate and a history's unit identifications; no return. None is adopted as a matched opening strength. The live zero is not measured absence.

claims.value: The frozen and live results read Union victory, and NPS says the Federals forced a retreat but failed to destroy or capture the Confederates. Price says Blunt was repulsed and driven three miles; Britton says Blunt's two brigades were driven back about a mile and were saved by Sanborn's arrival, after which the Confederates left the field.
claims.rationale: Retain the original result and engagement interval; later movements and campaign contribution are different measures. No new probabilities or individual causal credit.

open_questions: Blunt's (No. 80), Ford's, Jennison's and Sanborn's (No. 33) reports and Shelby's report remain deferred.

Rosecrans's, Pleasonton's and Curtis's reports, the subordinate Union and Confederate reports in Volume XLI Part 1, the organization of Price's army (No. 89), Maclean's itinerary (No. 90), the Price Court of Inquiry, Hinton's 1865 Rebel Invasion of Missouri and Kansas, maps and returns remain deferred.

NPS/CWSAC is one family (the NPS battle page plus the frozen Arnold rows). Wiley Britton's The Civil War on the Border, volume II (Putnam, 1899) is a retrospective history by a Union participant; by its preface the larger operations are based mainly on the published official reports, so it is not independent of the Price report family. Price's September 19 and November 2 dispatches and his December 28, 1864 report (Official Records Series I, Volume XLI, Part 1, No. 88) are one family of interested Confederate accounts. The Official Records volume is a shared container, not an additional witness. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting.
